ABSTRACT
Large-scale healthcare systems face significant challenges in ensuring security and privacy when sharing vast amounts of data
across various e-health entities. Existing studies often struggle with high processing costs, latency, energy consumption, and
delayed response times. To address these issues, this research proposes a novel Blockchain-Assisted Improved Puma Edge Comput-
ing Network (BA-IPEN) for efficient and secure healthcare data management. The proposed model integrates three key modules:
data collection at the IoT layer, data processing at the edge layer, and data storage at the cloud layer. Patient physiological data are
gathered from IoT sensors and transmitted to edge devices through remote gateway devices. At the edge layer, a Modified Puma
Optimization Algorithm (POA) is employed to maximize resource utilization while minimizing energy consumption and latency.
Additionally, edge computing performs preprocessing tasks such as missing data filtering and normalization to extract valuable
insights from raw sensor data, thereby enhancing overall performance. For secure data storage, the Blockchain-Assisted TwoFish
Algorithm is used. This algorithm encrypts collected data, bolstering security. Blockchain technology ensures tamper-proof
records and transparent access restrictions by providing a decentralized and immutable ledger for securely storing healthcare
data in the cloud. Extensive experiments demonstrate the effectiveness of the BA-IPEN model, revealing significant reductions
in computational cost and latency for cloud-based healthcare data storage. Experimental results also confirm the superiority
of the BA-IPEN model over traditional mechanisms, showcasing improvements in performance indicators and reduced energy
consumption.

These gadgets have sensors that monitor a variety of vital signs,
including body temperature, level of glucose, blood pressure,
weight, and heart rate, in addition to tracking physical activ-
ity. An IoT device is linked to a central cloud that manages
and stores data, in addition to facilitating device communica-
tion. Real-time patient tracking made possible by the IoT signif-
icantly reduces the need for doctors and actions [8]. IoT sensor
integration with edge computing allows for local data analysis
and processing, which lowers latency and lowers the possibil-
ity of data breaches brought on by sending sensitive data over
networks.
Additionally, edge computing enables instant reaction and
decision-making, which is essential in time-sensitive health-
care situations. Healthcare providers improve patient care and
treatment outcomes in real-time by gaining access to action-
able insights through data processing at the edge network [9].
However, even with edge computing’s benefits, maintaining the
accuracy and unchangeability of medical care is still a difficult
task. A Blockchain is utilized to manage data securely in cloud
connectivity and data acquisition. Healthcare centers guarantee
the provenance and integrity of data throughout its lifecycle by
employing Blockchain as a distributed ledger. It has been discov-
ered that a Blockchain-based digital EHR system provides safe
patient record storage in addition to a safe exchange of records
between verified, identified users via its smart contract-based
architecture.
Blockchain solutions are costly, even if they provide records with
immutable storage. Therefore, for the purpose of actually storing
records, an off-chain storage system like the Interplanetary File
system (IPFS) is added to a Blockchain-based system [10]. Health-
care data management has undergone a paradigm shift with the
combination of IoT sensors, edge computing, and blockchain
technology, which offers previously unheard-of levels of security,
efficiency, and transparency. In diverse edge computing environ-
ments, Blockchain’s mining and replication operations guaran-
tee accurate, consistent, and legitimate transactions by fusing all
these technologies. Furthermore, edge computing establishes a
private, autonomous setting where blockchain delegates storage
responsibilities to edge network servers and satisfies their storage
needs.

Motivation
This research is driven to work on emerging technologies such
as edge computing and IoT on the basis of outcomes that address
access control and data privacy preservation concerns with the
least amount of processing time and latency. Thus, two impor-
tant goals for healthcare data management are outlined in this
research. The primary goal is to decrease latency, processing
time, and reaction time while preserving the privacy of the data
acquired in the edge server and making crucial treatment deci-
sions for patients. Ensuring access to sensitive Patients’ Health
Information (PHI) that is kept in public storage is another
goal. Controlled access to PHI makes dealing with unauthorized
users easy.

Problem Solution
The research aims to implement an intermediary edge comput-
ing layer, where big amounts of data are processed in cloud
data centers and little data is gathered and analyzed at edge
devices for fast decision-making. By processing data close to
the data centers (healthcare network), this edge computing
layer lowers transmission costs and facilitates better structural
decision-making. The healthcare data management framework’s
security and privacy concerns are resolved by the intermediary
layer, which also speeds up processing, minimizing latency, and
reduces the workload associated with computing and communi-
cation. The Blockchain-assisted Two Fish algorithm is applied to
store healthcare data on the cloud securely. Here, the Two Fish
algorithm has a 128-bit encryption block size, and it is responsi-
ble for encrypting the gathered data. Also, this algorithm assists
in enhancing security.

Literature Review
This section examines numerous prior healthcare data man-
agement systems in edge computing, IoT, and Blockchain
techniques. This section covers various research analyses and
difficulties in previous studies. Abbas et al. [11] presented
a Blockchain-assisted secure data management framework
(BSDMF) for exchanging patient data securely in the health-
care environment. Secure data management and transmission
were ensured by applying blockchain among connected devices.
This approach provided better results and trust value. The Ellip-
tical Curve Diffie-Hellman (ECDH) technique was suggested
by Kumar et al. [12] for securely sharing clinical data in the
cloud environment. The encryption algorithm of the AES client
side was employed to perform the End-to-end file encryption to
ensure security in third-party cloud servers. This method offered
better security to securely save medical records in the cloud. How-
ever, this approach consumed more uploading time for patients’
clinical files.
For securely managing healthcare data, the encryption scheme of
Lionized remora optimization-based serpent (LRO-S) was devel-
oped by Almalawi et al. [13]. This approach reduced cyber-attacks
and privacy breaches from unauthorized users to encrypt sensi-
tive information, and it enhanced adaptability and safety. This
approach utilized IoT-sensed COVID patients’ information col-
lected from various remote places to guarantee data transmis-
sion securely. However, this method did not protect other disease
patient’s information. In the healthcare sector, Sharma et al. [14]
discussed a cloud computing technique for addressing issues of
managing vast data in the healthcare environment. This tech-
nique enhanced the maintenance of large volumes of data and
analytics. The adaptation of the cloud computing technique was
applied to save and manage data effectively, consume low cost,
and prevent physical servers. However, there is no proper solu-
tion that improves data protection regulations.
Azbeg et al. [15] suggested BlockMedCare for securely managing
data in the healthcare system. To guarantee security, blockchain,
and re-encryption proxy were utilized to save hash data. Access
control was implemented using smart contracts and employing
a proof of authority to expedite the data storage procedure. Data
was stored by using the Interplanetary File System (IPFS), and
blockchain ensured secure data transmission. This method pro-
vided a better improvement in the security of the healthcare
system, but it did not support data analysis and prevention of
data leakage. Optimized data management with secured feder-
ated learning (ODMSM-FL) was suggested by Ramani et al. [16]
to improve data management facilities in IoMT applications. The
ODMSM-FL technique solved security problems and maintained
data management facilities like data privacy, adequate storage,
and secure medical data transmission. This method obtained a
better security rate of 88.97% in IoMT applications; however, this
approach provided poor performance outcomes.
Blockchain-based Electronic health record (EHR) model was
developed by Sonkamble et al. [17] for secure EHR data trans-
mission. To save the EHR data securely, this system kept the
patient at the center of control. To avoid unauthorized users, EHR
transactions and access policies were implemented using secure
password authentication on the basis of key exchange (SPAKE)
protocol. This method provided secure EHR transactions. Nev-
ertheless, this model did not support user classification accord-
ing to interactions and behaviors. Jakhar et al. [18] established
a privacy-preserving access control model to ensure the security
of EHR. Due to irreversibility and immutability features, transac-
tions were safeguarded by blockchain technology. HyperLedger
Fabric was applied to implement access control between different
participants. This method efficiently developed security policies
and guaranteed the privacy and confidentiality of EHR data, but
it did not perform as a user-friendly healthcare framework.
Chang et al. [19] analyzed a lightweight authenticated encryp-
tion technique to encrypt the PHI data and protect the iden-
tity of biomedical sensors (BMS). The clinical data’s confiden-
tiality and authenticity were guaranteed by the adopted encryp-
tion mechanism. This method provided competitive performance
with respect to computational costs and Communication over-
heads. A Blockchain-assisted IoT-Edge system was developed by
ElRahman and Alluhaidan [20] to securely exchange healthcare
services. This system delivered all the characteristics of various
healthcare facilities, including safe transfer of patient examina-
tion outcomes and total protection of patient data. The Hyper-
ledger fabric platform was applied to solve security issues. This
technique obtained acceptable effectiveness and effectively acted
as user-friendly; however, it provided a poor security rate. The

IOT Architecture for Healthcare System
Billions of resource-constrained devices are anticipated to be con-
nected to the Internet as a result of the widespread implemen-
tation of IoT. Most of these gadgets, including implanted medi-
cal sensors and wearable sensors, cannot save the data that they
produce. For processing, this data is sent to the cloud by using
a straightforward design strategy. The latency of the cloud con-
nection is substantial due to the numerous devices that are con-
nected. Furthermore, these devices are not directly compatible
with the cloud architecture due to their limited power and band-
width. The transition to a more responsive design and hierar-
chical system architecture is important with the advent of edge
computing. The smart e-health gateway’s idea is to offer various
services at the IoT edge, connecting with smart medical sensors
and the cloud. The system architecture comprising the IoT layer,
edge layer, and cloud layer is portrayed in Figure 1.

IoT Layer
This phase includes the network equipment, medical IoT devices,
and resources that are used to sense and gather biological data
about patient’s information. Vital signs such as blood pressure,
blood cholesterol, and heart rate as well as other necessary biolog-
ical data are gathered from the patient. These signals are detected
by placing sensors in the patient’s clothing or body through the
body area network. After that, the data is sent to the gateway
by employing wired and wireless communication protocols like
Wi-Fi, 6LoWPAN, or ZigBee, and Bluetooth.

Edge Layer
The edge gateway layer sits in between the medical devices
and the cloud. Its work is to gather the unprocessed data
from clinical devices and transfer it to the cloud so that the
abnormalities in the patient are identified. Relocating data pro-
cessing closer to the network edge enables more energy effi-
ciency and quicker reaction times, which is the main notion
behind edge computing. Data mining and processing are done
on edge devices and servers that are nearer to the consumer
rather than continuously transferring data to the cloud for
computational functions, which helps to compute the energy
expenses. Moreover, it allows emergency medical assistance
to be delivered promptly in circumstances involving health
monitoring due to the short latency caused by edge solu-
tions. It contains IoT gateways that handle several wireless and
wired network access protocols like Bluetooth, Wi-Fi, and oth-
ers. With the ability to examine real-time data streams from
IoT sensors applied in medical equipment, patient wearables,

Cloud Layer
Intelligent processing is one of the characteristics of the IoT,
which stores vast volumes of data safely for intelligent data man-
agement. This is accomplished through the use of cloud comput-
ing and other intelligent computing technologies. In the system
design, a centralized cloud plays a major role in maintaining the
patient database and all of its medical features throughout time
and retrieving data when the application needs it. To improve
privacy, a proxy server is utilized to connect the edge gateway to
the cloud layer. After a predetermined amount of time, the edge
gateway uploads the sensor data to the cloud. In the event that
the edge gateway requires additional patient data, it retrieves the
information from the cloud. Blockchain technology guarantees
tamper-proof records and transparent access controls by offering
a decentralized and immutable ledger to save healthcare infor-
mation. In the healthcare ecosystem, the confidentiality princi-

authorized stakeholders. One way to secure data on the IoT is
through cryptography. The most effective instrument for imple-

Proposed Methodology
The proposed BA-IPEN model is developed to solve critical chal-
lenges in secure and effective healthcare data management, and
the architecture of BA-IPEN is depicted in Figure 2. The BA-IPEN
model integrates IoT, edge computing, and blockchain, along
with advanced optimization techniques. The BA-IPEN model
ensures the efficient collection, processing, and storage of health-
care data while decreasing latency and energy consumption and
improving data security. The edge layer bridges the gap between
IoT devices and cloud systems, which enables localized data pro-
cessing to minimize latency and improve resource utilization.
The edge layer carries out two key preprocessing tasks, including
filtering missing and noisy data, and normalization. The Kalman
filtering technique is applied to eliminate inconsistencies, noise,
and missing values, which ensures the integrity of the data. Addi-
tional filters, such as ReplaceMissing and RemoveUseless, refine
the dataset by replacing missing values with mean or median
estimates and discarding attributes with high variance. The
Z-score normalization is applied to scale the data. This prevents

Real-Time Data Collection
The proposed healthcare system collects physiological data from
patients, including blood sugar/glucose level, cholesterol level,
heart rate, blood oxygen, electrocardiogram (ECG), blood pres-
sure (BP), electroencephalogram (EEG), respiration rate, activity,
and electromyogram (EMG) through routine healthcare monitor-
ing. These data are sent to the edge devices, where disease predic-
tion and data pre-processing are done via remote gateway devices
like Bluetooth or Zigbee. This provides insightful data for making
final decisions, which is subsequently saved in a cloud database.

Edge Computing With Data Analytical
Engine
Data analysis and computation for IoT services are provided by
one promising technology called edge computing, which operates
at the edge network. Offloading computational tasks and local
data created by IoT devices to edge nodes greatly lowers latency
and increases IoT service reliability. The primary goals of edge
computing are as follows:
• Decreasing the response time delay’s long-term average
while taking into consideration limitations is the consump-
tion of power and computation resources.
• Enhancing data management to handle massive volumes of
UE-created, potentially delay-sensitive data that need to be
processed in real-time.
• Due to the lesser quantity of network resources accessible at
cloud edges compared to the cloud, resource management is
enhanced to maximize the application of network resources,
hence enhancing network effectiveness.
Here, this research proposes a novel data stream processing struc-
ture, which carefully distributes the computing and network
resources accessible at the edge to maximize the effectiveness
of stream processing usage. In order to lower response times
and network backbone traffic, the optimization algorithm inves-
tigates the idle edge device resources for task execution.

It is important to protect the integrity of data gathered among
the sensor layer, in the IoT healthcare area, in which the col-
lected information is encrypted using the Two Fish technique.
The Two Fish technique is appealing because of its exceptional
performance and versatility, which make it appropriate for a wide
range of platforms. Its boosted security and wider applicability
are due to its 128-bit encryption block size and support for up
to 256-bit key lengths. Two Fish’s versatility enables it to process
well on a variety of platforms, including 32-bit central processing
units (CPUs) and 8-bit smart cards, and it is suitable for tiny and
large-scale circuits. Different performance levels are supported
by its architecture, which is impacted by 176 hardware specifi-
cations, the size of the key, encryption process speed, and mem-
ory needs. It is commonly known that the Two Fish technique is
effective in cryptographic applications.

ers and users in order to execute decryption and encryption
techniques. Blockchain is employed to record each contract call.

reputated and is not tampered with.

Conclusion
Healthcare data management is increasingly greatly concerned
with security and privacy concerns. In order to prevent these
issues, this research proposes a novel BA-IPEN model, which
offers safe and efficient storage of healthcare data in the cloud.
The patient’s physiological information is collected via an IoT
sensor and remote gateway devices are applied to send this
data to edge devices. In edge computing, data is processed on
edge devices or servers that are nearer to the user, in which
the Puma optimizer is employed to optimize task distribution
and management of energy, thus decreasing latency and energy
usage. Edge computing executes preprocessing procedures, in
which filtering out missing information is performed by the
Kalman filtering strategy, and to enhance the convergence rate
the z-score standardization approach is applied to normalize the
data. This research employs a new Blockchain-assisted Two Fish
algorithm, where the gathered data is encrypted using the Two
Fish algorithm for the safe storage of healthcare information.
Moreover, the encrypted file information is saved on the cloud
using smart contracts. Overall, the BA-IPEN offers enhanced
data processing efficiency, bolstered data security, and optimized
response time, latency, energy consumption, resource utiliza-
tion, and throughput in the management of healthcare data. The
BA-IPEN model for healthcare data management only involves
the secure storage process of healthcare data in the cloud, and in
the future, this research plans to explore data sharing and other
data management-related processes.

Abstract: Large-scale healthcare systems face significant challenges in ensuring security and privacy when sharing vast amounts of data across various e-health entities. Existing studies often struggle with high processing costs, latency, energy consumption, and delayed response times. To address these issues, this research proposes a novel Blockchain-Assisted Improved Puma Edge Comput- ing Network (BA-IPEN) for efficient and secure healthcare data management. The proposed model integrates three key modules: data collection at the IoT layer, data processing at the edge layer, and data storage at the cloud layer. Patient physiological data are gathered from IoT sensors and transmitted to edge devices through remote gateway devices. At the edge layer, a Modified Puma Optimization Algorithm (POA) is employed to maximize resource utilization while minimizing energy consumption and latency. Additionally, edge computing performs preprocessing tasks such as missing data filtering and normalization to extract valuable insights from raw sensor data, thereby enhancing overall performance. For secure data storage, the Blockchain-Assisted TwoFish Algorithm is used. This algorithm encrypts collected data, bolstering security. Blockchain technology ensures tamper-proof records and transparent access restrictions by providing a decentralized and immutable ledger for securely storing healthcare data in the cloud. Extensive experiments demonstrate the effectiveness of the BA-IPEN model, revealing significant reductions in computational cost and latency for cloud-based healthcare data storage. Experimental results also confirm the superiority of the BA-IPEN model over traditional mechanisms, showcasing improvements in performance indicators and reduced energy consumption.
